Power decomposition analysis (strict evolutionary MTM band-power ratio)

Source: R/pda.R
pda.Rd

The pda function calculates, in moving windows, the ratio between the multitaper (MTM) power inside a set of target frequency bands and the power inside a total frequency band (power decomposition analysis, PDA; Li et al., 2016). Each window is linearly detrended, its adaptive-weighted MTM power spectral density is computed on an explicit FFT grid, and band powers are obtained by trapezoidal integration of the PSD with piecewise-linear interpolation at the exact band limits. The input is divided by one global scale (maximum absolute value) so that powers are comparable between windows. The data must already be regularly sampled (relative spacing tolerance 1e-5); no sorting, interpolation or padding is performed. Defaults for step, nfft and total_band follow the Acycle compatibility wrapper pda.m (one sample interval, next power of two of the window length, DC to Nyquist). Translated from Acycle v3.1 acyclePowerDecomposition.m and pda.m (Mingsong Li).

Usage

pda(
  data = NULL,
  target_bands = c(1/45, 1/25),
  window = 500,
  step = NULL,
  nw = 2,
  nfft = NULL,
  total_band = NULL,
  genplot = FALSE,
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

Numeric two-column matrix or data frame: depth/time in column 1 (strictly increasing and evenly spaced, relative spacing tolerance 1e-5; interpolate first if needed) and the proxy value in column 2; at least eight rows, all values finite. Required (Default=NULL).

target_bands

Target frequency bands whose summed power is divided by the power of total_band, in cycles per unit of the depth/time column: either a B x 2 matrix with the lower limit in column 1 and the upper limit in column 2 (rows ordered by increasing lower limit, non-overlapping), or a numeric vector of paired limits c(lower1, upper1, lower2, upper2, ...). Every band must lie inside total_band, below the Nyquist frequency and be at least as wide as the FFT resolution. Default=c(1/45, 1/25).

window

Length of the moving window (first-to-last coordinate span), in the unit of the depth/time column (numeric, > 0 and not longer than the record; rounded to a whole number of sample intervals, at least 8 samples). Default=500.

step

Distance between the starts of successive windows, in the unit of the depth/time column (numeric, > 0; rounded to whole samples). NULL uses one sample interval. Default=NULL.

nw

Time-bandwidth product of the DPSS (Slepian) tapers of the multitaper spectrum (numeric, >= 0.5 and less than half the number of samples per window); larger values smooth the spectrum more. Default=2.

nfft

Length of the FFT (even integer, at least the number of samples per window); larger values give a finer frequency grid. NULL uses the next power of two of the number of samples per window. Default=NULL.

total_band

Total frequency band c(lower, upper) in cycles per unit of the depth/time column (numeric vector of length 2, 0 <= lower < upper <= Nyquist frequency), the denominator of the power ratio. NULL uses c(0, Nyquist frequency). Default=NULL.

genplot

Plot the data and the power ratio against depth/time (logical, TRUE or FALSE). Default=FALSE.

verbose

Show a progress bar over the windows (logical, TRUE or FALSE). Default=FALSE.

Value

A list with elements result: matrix with columns window center, ratio (target power / total power), target power (union of all target bands) and total power; band_powers: matrix with the window center followed by one power column per target band; meta: list with the resolved sampling interval, window and step samples, effective window/step lengths, nfft, frequency resolution, Nyquist frequency, value scale and number of unused trailing samples.

References

Li, M., Huang, C., Hinnov, L., Ogg, J., Chen, Z.-Q., Zhang, Y., 2016. Obliquity-forced climate during the Early Triassic hothouse in China. Geology 44, 623-626. doi:10.1130/G37970.1

Li, M., Hinnov, L., Kump, L., 2019. Acycle: Time-series analysis software for paleoclimate research and education. Computers & Geosciences 127, 12-22. doi:10.1016/j.cageo.2019.02.011

Author

Michiel Arts (R translation); original MATLAB code: Mingsong Li and Linda Hinnov (Acycle).

Examples

# \donttest{
set.seed(1)
t <- seq(0, 2000, by = 2)
x <- sin(2 * pi * t / 40) + 0.5 * sin(2 * pi * t / 100) +
  0.5 * as.numeric(arima.sim(list(ar = 0.7), n = length(t)))
res <- pda(data = cbind(t, x), target_bands = c(1/45, 1/35),
  window = 300, step = 10, nw = 2, genplot = FALSE)
head(res$result)
#>      center     ratio target_power total_power
#> [1,]    150 0.3611018   0.02865209  0.07934631
#> [2,]    160 0.3383209   0.02810777  0.08308022
#> [3,]    170 0.3086794   0.02743037  0.08886362
#> [4,]    180 0.2902889   0.02847236  0.09808285
#> [5,]    190 0.2774705   0.02849600  0.10269921
#> [6,]    200 0.2786652   0.02890460  0.10372519
# }
